title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Ranking the Favorites to Win the Yashin Trophy
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath, Barnaby LaneSep 8, 2026Vozinha continues to get his flowers. / Ju Huanzong/Xinhua/Getty ImagesTen goalkeepers have made the shortlist for the 2026 Yashin Trophy.
The award—named after the legendary Lev Yashin and seen as the top individual honor for keepers—was created by France Football in 2019 as part of an expansion of their annual Ballon d’Or ceremony.

Gianluigi Donnarumma lifted the prize for the second time last year after his heroics with Paris Saint-Germain but is not even among the nominees this time around with the winner to be crowned in London on Oct. 26.
Here’s a breakdown of 2026’s runners and riders, ranked by their likelihood of taking home the trophy.

Yassine Bounou shone again on the world stage. / Issam Zerrok/Hans Lucas/AFP/Getty ImagesClub: Al HilalHonors: King’s Cup, Africa Cup of NationsBounou proved he’s still got it at the age of 35, putting in some showreel performances at the summer’s World Cup as Morocco reached the quarterfinals.Prior to that he, technically, became an Africa Cup of Nations winner at the start of this year—winning the Golden Glove at the home tournament.He also bagged a King’s Cup with his club side in Saudi Arabia.

Courtois did not enjoy his finest year. / Alex Caparros/Getty ImagesClub: Real MadridHonors: N/ACourtois remains one of the finest goalkeepers in world soccer, but the 2025–26 season fell short of his usual standards.Real Madrid endured another trophyless campaign, with Courtois missing a crucial stretch of the season through injury in the spring. His absence underlined just how important the Belgian is to the team.Belgium suffered a similar setback at the World Cup. The Red Devils’ quarterfinal against Spain ended in defeat after Courtois was forced off with an injury.

Mendy is a former Yashin Trophy runner-up. / Yasser Bakhsh/Getty ImagesClub: Al AhliHonors: AFC Champions LeagueEdouard Mendy has continued to build an impressive trophy collection, winning back-to-back AFC Champions League titles and keeping a clean sheet in the 2025–26 final.The Senegalese goalkeeper also claimed the Saudi Pro League Golden Glove in 2026, further strengthening his reputation as one of the best shot-stoppers currently playing outside Europe.He also made headlines on the international stage—featuring in the controversial Africa Cup of Nations final, saving Brahim Díaz’s late penalty.

All eyes were on Vozinha this summer. / Maddie Meyer/FIFA/Getty ImagesClub: Chaves/Colo-ColoHonors: N/AWere France Football to introduce an award for best social media growth, Vozinha would be a shoo-in.The 40-year-old went from being a little-known keeper at the tail end of his career to having nearly 30 million followers on Instagram in the space of a few weeks this summer.His acrobatic performances for Cabo Verde at the World Cup catapulted him into the spotlight and helped his side reach the round of 32—they ultimately exited the competition without losing a game in 90 minutes.

Martínez is hoping for his third Yashin Trophy win. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images Club: Aston Villa/ChelseaHonors: Europa LeagueIt’s been another big season for Martínez, who won the Europa League with Aston Villa, played in his second World Cup final with Argentina and earned a transfer to Chelsea.Still, the two-time previous winner of the Yashin Trophy is probably not among the big favorites for the award this year. While his save percentage in 2025–26 stood at an impressive 70.9%, he ranked just 15th for clean sheets in the Premier League.

Kobel lit up the Bundesliga and World Cup. / IMAGO/Nicolo CampoClub: Borussia DortmundHonors: N/AKobel also made his mark at the 2026 World Cup, keeping two clean sheets as Switzerland reached the quarterfinals.Only two goalkeepers recorded more saves than the Swiss international in North America, and he proved decisive in the round-of-16 shootout win over Colombia, saving Cucho Hernández’s penalty to help send his country through.His club form was just as impressive. He kept 15 clean sheets in the Bundesliga during the 2025–26 season, more than any other goalkeeper.

Matvey Safonov has made PSG’s transition from Gianluigi Donnarumma appear seamless. / Jose Hernandez/Anadolu via Getty ImagesClub: PSGHonors: Ligue 1, Champions League, UEFA Super CupBrought in initially as a backup option, Safonov has grown in stature at Paris Saint-Germain, eventually convincing Luis Enrique of his credentials as the man to inherit the position as the club’s first-choice goalkeeper following Donnarumma’s departure.The Russian made key saves during the defending champions’ Champions League run—particularly in a barnstorming semifinal against Bayern Munich.

David Raya was near-unbeatable at times in 2025-26. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesClub: ArsenalHonors: Premier League, World CupIt was a another stellar season for Raya, who claimed his third straight Premier League Golden Glove, while keeping 19 clean sheets and conceding just 26 goals in 2025–26.His presence, reflexes and distribution proved key foundations for Mikel Arteta’s near-unbeatable defense as they claimed the Premier League title for first time in over 20 years.The Spaniard was also named in the Champions League Team of the Season and was part of Spain’s victorious World Cup squad—though didn’t feature.

Barcelona struck gold with Joan García.  / Pablo Rodriguez/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesClub: BarcelonaHonors: La Liga, Supercopa de España, World CupGarcía enjoyed a superb debut season at Barcelona after making the cross-city switch from Espanyol, quickly establishing himself as one of Spain’s standout goalkeepers.He helped Barça win La Liga and collected two individual honors along the way: the Zamora Trophy, awarded to the league’s best goalkeeper, and the Save of the Season award.García’s numbers backed up the accolades. His 77.9% save rate was the highest of any goalkeeper in the competition during the 2025–26 campaign.Although he spent the 2026 World Cup on the bench, García still earned a winners’ medal as part of Spain’s title-winning squad.

Unai Simón was awarded the Golden Glove at the World Cup. / Erick W. Rasco/Sports IllustratedClub: Athletic ClubHonors: World CupWith plenty of options at his disposal ahead of the 2026 World Cup, Spain manager Luis de la Fuente remained loyal to Unai Simón, keeping him as his first-choice goalkeeper despite a relatively quiet season at club level.That faith paid off spectacularly. The Athletic Club star delivered a historic tournament, conceding just once in eight appearances as Spain went on to lift the trophy.Simón recorded seven clean sheets in North America, setting a new World Cup record and earning the Golden Glove award.
